_README: Divergences between the MySQL and DuckDB execution engines that are ACCOUNTED
FOR, so the engine A/B gate can fail on the ones that are not.
This baseline is separate from duck/known-divergences.json in the rvf repo,
and started empty. That one classifies a Python engine against a production
MySQL report - different corpus, different host, different release. This one
classifies two instances of ONE jar, on one host, validating one release,
with only rvf.execution.engine differing. The causes are not the same, so
inheriting its allowances would import excuses that do not apply.
An entry is a claim that a difference is UNDERSTOOD, not that it is
acceptable. Each needs a direction, what it applies to, the cause, and the
evidence for that cause - a file and line, a measurement, or a reproduction.
'Both engines have always done this' is not evidence.
The point is for this file to shrink. An entry removed because the underlying
defect was fixed belongs in removedAllowances with the commit that fixed it,
Keys are assertion UUIDs, because that is what the gate looks up. The slug field carries the human name.

directions.candidate-higher: DuckDB reports more failures than MySQL for an assertion
directions.incumbent-higher: MySQL reports more failures than DuckDB for an assertion

02cf4438-170e-4b6b-b5da-624ef730a8e0.appliesTo: file-centric-snapshot-inactivated-component-module, on any release that ships an Identifier file
02cf4438-170e-4b6b-b5da-624ef730a8e0.observed: MySQL failureCount -1 in assertionsWarning; DuckDB 0 in assertionsPassed
cause: The assertion calls validate_inactivated_component_module, whose cursor is
'select table_name from information_schema.tables ... and table_name like
'%\_d'' - every delta table in the schema - and the dynamic SQL it builds
identifier_d has no id column. RF2 identifies those rows by
'Unknown column t1.id in field list' and the whole assertion is abandoned.
The DuckDB engine does not iterate at runtime: publish_store.py unrolls the
procedure into one statement per table, and the unroller enumerated the 52
tables that actually have an id. identifier_d is not among them, so the
assertion runs over the tables it can answer for.
evidence: MySQL report failureMessage: 'Error executing SQL command object Nested
exception : java.sql.SQLSyntaxErrorException: Unknown column t1.id in field list'
The store's unrolled form of 02cf4438 holds 56 statements over 52 tables and
does not name identifier_s or identifier_d - checked directly against
identifier_d exists in MySQL only because create-tables-mysql.sql now creates
it: it is one of the 12 tables added by the RF2-file-types change (fork PR #23,
IHTSDO #74). Before that change the cursor never saw it.
notThePlan: This is recorded so the gate is usable, NOT because the behaviour is right.
MySQL abandoning the assertion means it validates nothing on an AU release,
and the fix belongs in the assertions corpus: the cursor should skip tables
with no id column. Raised as a finding against IHTSDO #74, which is what
02cf4438-170e-4b6b-b5da-624ef730a8e0.directionNote: MySQL -1 against DuckDB 0, so the tool reads it as candidate-higher. The arithmetic is on the sentinel, not on findings: MySQL abandoned the assertion and DuckDB executed it and found nothing.

26c25479-c3ba-47f2-9851-bb05ae42ad48.appliesTo: any assertion whose SQL names <PREVIOUS> or <DEPENDENCY> when that release was not supplied to the run
26c25479-c3ba-47f2-9851-bb05ae42ad48.observed: DuckDB failureCount -1 with 'Not run: requires <DEPENDENCY>, which was not supplied to this validation'; MySQL 0 in assertionsPassed
cause: MySqlQueryTransformer drops any statement still naming a release the run does
not hold. The assertion then executes with fewer statements, finds nothing,
and is reported as PASSED - a pass for work that was never attempted.
DuckBinder mirrors the drop but reports the assertion as not executed, which
is what -1 means. So DuckDB is the honest one here and the divergence is in
the incumbent's favour only in appearance.
evidence: this run supplied previousRelease and no dependencyRelease.
Same mechanism as the 53 assertions that carry -1 on a first-time release
while MySQL reports them passed - measured on the AU edition.
notThePlan: A pass that means 'not attempted' is the more dangerous of the two
behaviours. The DuckDB side needs no change; the reporting gap is worth
raising with SI separately, since Release-Dashboard-UI renders -1 literally.
26c25479-c3ba-47f2-9851-bb05ae42ad48.directionNote: MySQL 0 against DuckDB -1, so the tool reads it as incumbent-higher. Again the sentinel, not findings: MySQL passed an assertion it never fully ran and DuckDB declined to.

_README: Assertions one engine reports that do not join to the other by assertionUuid.
Zero is the target: both engines read the same corpus, so a missing join is
an assertion one of them silently did not run.
